{{Short description|FIFA World Cup group}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2025}}
{{Use American English|date=November 2025}}
Group D of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] took place from June 12 to 25, 2026.<ref name="match schedule">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 26 – Match Schedule |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=February 4, 2024}}</ref> The group consisted of the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] (co-host), [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]], [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]], and [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]]. This also marked the return of Turkey and Paraguay to the World Cup finals, their first appearances since [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002]] and [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]] respectively.

The United States were the second team to secure their place in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]] after Mexico, and were guaranteed to top the group after two consecutive wins. Australia finished in second place, edging out Paraguay based on head-to-head goal difference. Paraguay's performance allowed them to advance as one of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|eight best third-place teams]],<ref name="regulations">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 Regulations |publisher=FIFA |date=May 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623212158/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> and would further advance into the round of 16 (all other third-place teams were eliminated by then). 

Turkey exited the tournament after two consecutive defeats but managed to beat co-hosts the United States in their final group match.

==Standings==
{{2026 FIFA World Cup group tables|Group D}}

In the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]]:<ref name="regulations"/>
* The winner of Group D, the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]], advanced to play the third-place team of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group B|Group B]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]].
* The runner-up of Group D, [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]], advanced to play the runner-up of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group G|Group G]], [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]].
* The third-place team of Group D, [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]], advanced to play the winner of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group E|Group E]], [[Germany national football team|Germany]], as one of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|eight best third-place teams]] from the group stage.

===United States vs Paraguay===
[[File:2026 FIFA World Cup Match 4, United States v Paraguay (1).jpg|thumb|right|160px|During the United States vs. Paraguay match at [[SoFi Stadium]]]]

The teams had met nine times previously, including once in the World Cup, a 3–0 victory in the [[1930 FIFA World Cup Group 4#United States vs Paraguay|group stage]] for the United States in [[1930 FIFA World Cup|1930]], and most recently in 2025, a 2–1 win for the United States in a friendly. This match marked the United States' second victory on home soil, the other being 2–1 win over [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]] in the [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] edition.<ref>{{cite web|title=United States national football team: record v Paraguay|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/usa/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Paraguay|website=11v11.com|access-date=June 12, 2026}}</ref>

The United States went in front in the 7th minute when [[Damián Bobadilla]] stuck his foot out and inadvertently put the ball in his own net after a low from the left by [[Weston McKennie]]. It was 2–0 in the 31st minute when [[Folarin Balogun]] scored with a low side foot finish to the right after a pass from [[Christian Pulisic]] on the left. Balogun got his second goal of the game in added time in the first half when he scored with a left-footed shot to the top left corner of the net after cutting in from the right.
[[Maurício (footballer, born 2001)|Maurício]] pulled a goal back for Paraguay in the 73rd minute with a low finish to the right of the net.
In the 98th minute, [[Giovanni Reyna]] made it 4–1 with a shot to the left of the net with the outside of his right leg from just inside the penalty area on the right.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c78y1jyknv1t|title= United States 4 Paraguay 1|date=13 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref>

With a brace, Folarin Balogun became the first American player to score more than once in a World Cup match since [[Bert Patenaude]] scored the tournament's first ever hat-trick in [[1930 FIFA World Cup|1930]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Folarin Balogun makes USMNT history not seen in 96 years vs. Paraguay in World Cup opener|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/fifa_world_cup/folarin-balogun-makes-usmnt-history-not-seen-in-96-years-vs-paraguay-in-world-cup-opener/ar-AA25xIHo|website=MSN|access-date=June 14, 2026}}</ref> This also marked the first time the United States ever scored four times in a World Cup match.<ref>{{cite web|title=USA Makes History With Its First Four-Goal Performance At Men's World Cup|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/usa-makes-history-its-first-four-goal-performance-mens-world-cup|website=Fox Sports|access-date=June 14, 2026}}</ref>

===Australia vs Turkey===
[[File:Australia vs Türkiye at BC Place - June 13, 2026.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[BC Place]] before the match]]

The teams had played against each other twice previously, with Turkey winning both friendly matches played in May 2004.<ref>{{cite web|title=Australia national football team: record v Turkey|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/australia/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Turkey/|website=11v11.com|access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref> This was the only match in Group D held outside of the [[West Coast of the United States]].

The fixture was Turkey's first World Cup game in 24 years,<ref name="guardianref">{{cite web|last1=Snape |first1=Jack |title=In their own words, Turkey are 'more talented' than Australia. Can the Socceroos spoil the party? – World Cup 2026 – The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/14/australia-socceroos-world-cup-turkey-preview-more-talented-spoil-the-party|website=www.theguardian.com|access-date=15 June 2026}}</ref> having reached the semi-finals in their previous appearance in [[2002 FIFA World Cup#Match for third place|2002]]. Turkey captain [[Hakan Çalhanoğlu]] described his side as "more talented" than Australia in a press conference prior to the game, and predicted his side would dominate the game.<ref name="guardianref"/> 

Socceroos coach [[Tony Popović]] made a controversial decision to drop seasoned goalkeeper and skipper [[Mathew Ryan]] from the starting lineup in favor of young goalkeeper [[Patrick Beach]].<ref>{{cite web|title=
World Cup: Socceroos down Türkiye with Nestory Irankunda and Connor Metcalfe's wondergoals|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-06-14/world-cup-live-updates-australia-vs-turkiye-socceroos/106796000|website=abc.net.au|access-date=15 June 2026}}</ref> In the 27th minute, [[Nestory Irankunda]] cut in from the left and scored with a low finish to the left to put Australia in the lead. Shortly after, Turkey almost equalized when a powerful strike by [[Abdülkerim Bardakcı|Abdülkerim Bardakçı]] was parried onto the post by Beach.<ref name="TheNewsAusTur">{{Cite web |website=The News| last=Sullivan |first=Matthew |date=15 June 2026 |title=Turkey captain doubles down on Socceroos slander in tense exchange with Aussie reporter |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/football/world-cup/we-didnt-dominate-turkey-captain-doubles-down-on-socceroos-slander/news-story/de92d82abd35269deb390b490d283741}}</ref>

In the second half, despite mounting pressure from Turkey, Aussie midfielder [[Connor Metcalfe]] made it 2–0 when he cut in from the right before shooting low to the right corner of the net from outside the penalty area.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn8kgrx2pl7t|title= Australia 2 Turkey 0|date=14 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12098/13552630/world-cup-2026-australia-2-0-turkey-socceroos-make-winning-start-to-group-d-campaign-in-vancouver|title= World Cup 2026: Australia 2–0 Turkey – Socceroos make winning start to Group D campaign in Vancouver|date=14 June 2026|work=Sky Sports|accessdate=16 June 2026}}</ref>

After the game, Çalhanoğlu maintained his team were better than Australia, regardless of the result. Irankunda, one of the goal scorers for Australia, admitted after the game that the comments were used as motivation by the Australian players.<ref name="TheNewsAusTur"/>

Regarded as an [[upset victory]], this was Australia's first win in an opening World Cup match since [[2006 FIFA World Cup Group F#Australia vs Japan|2006]], and their joint-largest overall victory to date.<ref>{{cite web|title=Socceroos stun Turkey in start to FIFA World Cup campaign|url=https://greekherald.com.au/sports/socceroos-stun-turkey-2-0-to-make-dream-start-to-fifa-world-cup-campaign/|website=The Greek Herald|access-date=14 June 2026}}</ref>

===United States vs Australia===
[[File:Tim Ream Australia v USA 19 June 2026-235.jpg|thumb|right|During the match between the United States and Australia]]
The teams have faced each other four times before the tournament, most recently in 2025, a 2–1 win for the United States in a friendly.<ref>{{cite web|title=United States national football team: record v Australia|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/usa/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Australia|website=11v11.com|access-date=5 December 2025}}</ref>

Australia applied some early pressure and [[Mohamed Touré (soccer, born 2004)|Mohamed Touré]] had a shot on goal after just 40 seconds, but it was comfortably saved by United States goalkeeper [[Matt Freese]].
[[Cameron Burgess]] committed an own goal in the 11th minute, and [[Alex Freeman]] headed the ball past [[Patrick Beach]] to make the score 2–0 just before halftime.<ref name="ABCNewsUSA-AUS">{{Cite web |website=ABC News| last1=Smale |first1=Simon |last2=Wildie | first2=Tom |date=20 June 2026 |title=Socceroos beaten 2-0 by USA in Seattle blockbuster |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-06-20/world-cup-socceroos-vs-usa-live-australia/106817274}}</ref>

Australia coach [[Tony Popovic]] made three changes at half time, including bringing on [[Nestory Irankunda]] and [[Connor Metcalfe]],  in an attempt to turn the game in Australia's favour. [[Cristian Volpato]] was later substituted on with half an hour left, replacing [[Mathew Leckie]], who had been struggling with a hamstring injury. Volpato managed a shot on goal which went over the crossbar, and later Metcalfe shot directly at Freese.<ref name="ABCNewsUSA-AUS"/>

Australia continued to struggle with creating any genuine chances throughout the match, and the United States comfortably defended their lead in the second half.<ref name="ABCNewsUSA-AUS"/> With the win, the United States officially qualified for the Round of 32, becoming the second team overall to do so after Mexico.

===Turkey vs Paraguay===
The teams have only met once before, in a scoreless draw of a friendly in 1995.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paraguay national football team: record v Turkey|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/paraguay/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Turkey/|website=11v11.com|access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref> 

Turkey's loss confirmed their elimination from the tournament due to the head-to-head tiebreaker, making them the second team to be knocked out after [[Haiti national football team|Haiti]], who became the first to be eliminated hours earlier following a [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group C#Brazil vs Haiti|3–0 defeat]] against Brazil in Philadelphia. This marked their first early exit from a major tournament since [[UEFA Euro 2020]], where they were also eliminated following [[UEFA Euro 2020 Group A|two consecutive defeats]]. The result also confirmed the United States as the winner of the group due to the same tiebreaker. It was also the first time that Turkey failed to score in two consecutive World Cup matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c2kyg22l2n7t|title=Turkey 0 Paraguay 1|date=20 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=25 June 2026}}</ref>

[[Miguel Almirón]] became the first player to be sent off under FIFA's new law prohibiting players from covering their mouths during confrontations with opponents, receiving a straight [[Penalty card#Red card|red card]] after a [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] review following an altercation with [[Mert Müldür]] in the stoppage time of the first half.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cartwright |first1=Phil |title=Almiron first player sent off for covering mouth |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvg58m7n1plo |website=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |access-date=20 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260620113940/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvg58m7n1plo |archive-date=20 June 2026 |date=20 June 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

With 32 shot attempts and no goals scored, Turkey surpassed Portugal’s [[2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#England vs Portugal|2006 quarter-final]] record of 31 shots for the most attempts in a single World Cup match without scoring. Combined with its 30 attempts against Australia, Turkey now holds the tournament record for the most shots without a goal across two consecutive matches, totaling 62 attempts.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hay |first=Phil |last2=Tharme |first2=Liam |date=20 June 2026 |title=How Turkey took 62 shots and scored no goals in World Cup's most miserable campaign |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7378854/2026/06/20/turkey-62-shots-0-goals-world-cup/ |access-date=14 July 2026 |work=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

After 64 seconds, [[Matías Galarza (Paraguayan footballer)|Matías Galarza]] scored with a low left-foot shot from outside the penalty area into the right corner of the net to put Paraguay in front. The goal was the fastest goal of the tournament to date, surpassing the previous record of 71 seconds set by Morocco's [[Ismael Saibari]] against [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] hours earlier [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group C#Scotland vs Morocco|in Boston]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=20 June 2026 |title=2026 World Cup: Hours after Morocco's Ismael Saibari delivers fastest goal, Paraguay's Matias Galarza sets new record |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/soccer/breaking-news/article/2026-world-cup-hours-after-moroccos-ismael-saibari-delivers-fastest-goal-paraguays-matias-galarza-sets-new-record-224107077.html |work=[[Yahoo Sports]]}}</ref>

===Turkey vs United States===
The teams had faced each other five times prior to the tournament, most recently in 2025, a 2–1 win for Turkey in a friendly.<ref>{{cite web|title=Turkey national football team: record v USA|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/turkey/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/USA/|website=11v11.com|access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>

The match was considered a "[[dead rubber]]", as after matchday two the United States were confirmed as group winners and Turkey were confirmed in fourth and eliminated due to the tiebreaker rules.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pelit |first=Asli |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7381805/2026/06/22/usmnt-turkey-world-cup-montella-pochettino/ |title=How Turkey's World Cup hopes fell apart – and rendered USMNT clash a dead rubber |publisher = New York Times |work= [[The Athletic]] |date=June 22, 2026 |access-date=June 23, 2026}}</ref> As a result, United States coach [[Mauricio Pochettino]] fielded almost a completely different side to that used in their opening two fixtures, featuring nine new starters.<ref name="ABC_Turkey_USA">{{Cite web |website=ABC News| last=McCarthy |first=Kelly |date=26 June 2026 |title=US men's team falls to Turkey 3-2, but still advancing to World Cup knockout round |url=https://abcnews.com/GMA/Culture/usmnt-world-cup-match-turkey-soccer/story?id=134198534}}</ref>

A dramatic stoppage-time goal by [[Kaan Ayhan]] secured Turkey's first World Cup match victory [[2002 FIFA World Cup#Match for third place|since 2002]] (when it finished third), and handed co-host United States its first defeat of the tournament. United States completed the group stage of the tournament with their best ever finish of 6 points from three matches,<ref name="ABC_Turkey_USA"/> and also with their highest World Cup goal tally of eight.<ref name="NBC_Turkey_USA">{{Cite web |website=NBC News| last=Greif |first=Andrew |date=26 June 2026 |title=The U.S. can shrug off its last-gasp loss to Turkey. Now the stakes go up. |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/sports/soccer/us-loses-3-2-turkey-bosnia-world-cup-knockouts-pulisic-rcna351879}}</ref> Had they won the game, it would have marked the first time any United States side had won three World Cup fixtures in a row.<ref name="ABC_Turkey_USA"/>

With this result, the United States had reached the knockout round in three of its last four attempts at the World Cup, with two exits in the round of 16, and a [[2002 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Germany vs United States|2002]] run to the quarterfinals that remains the national team's best performance, excluding finishing third in the first World Cup in [[1930 FIFA World Cup|1930]].<ref name="NBC_Turkey_USA"/>

Furthermore, this marked the second defeat for a tournament co-host, following Canada's [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group B#Switzerland vs Canada|2–1 loss]] to Switzerland the previous day in Vancouver. This leaves [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] as the only co-host to remain undefeated, having won all of their group stage matches.

===Paraguay vs Australia===
[[File:Levi%27s_Stadium_2026_FIFA_World_Cup_Australia_v._Paraguay.jpg|thumb|right|[[Levi's Stadium]] during the match]]
The teams had previously faced each other five times, most recently in 2010, a 1–0 win for Australia in a friendly match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Paraguay national football team: record v Australia|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/paraguay/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Australia|website=11v11.com|access-date=5 December 2025}}</ref>

The match ended in a scoreless draw, securing Australia second place in the group and also allowing Paraguay to advance the following day once enough third-place teams had finished with three points or less.

==Discipline==
The team conduct ("fair play") score would have been used as a tiebreaker if the head-to-head and overall records of teams were tied. It would also be used as a tiebreaker for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|third-place ranking]] between groups if the overall records of teams were tied. The score was calculated based on yellow and red cards received by players and team officials in all group matches as follows:<ref name="regulations"/>
*yellow card: −1 point;
*indirect red card (second yellow card): −3 points;
*direct red card: −4 points;
*yellow card and direct red card: −5 points;

Only one of the above deductions could be applied to a player or team official in a single match.
